races.title: State House, District 69
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Dean Arp
cands.bio: Larry Dean Arp Jr. is a licensed professional engineer and president of Arp Engineering in Monroe. He served over 12 years on the Union County school board. A Republican, he has represented North Carolina House District 69 (northwestern Union County) since 2013 and is Senior Chair of Appropriations.
cands.gaps: We found no documented positions from Arp on data centers, development or growth, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land purchases, immigration or H-1B, policing, guns, or teacher pay. His campaign site speaks generally of 'local control in education' and getting politicians out of the way of parents, but does not name vouchers, charters or school choice. His birthplace, where he was raised and when he moved to North Carolina are not stated in the pages we had. Ballotpedia lists no endorsements for him in 2026, and he did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate surveys, so there is little in his own words beyond his campaign site. We found no controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

cands.name: Heidi Sinsley
cands.bio: Heidi Sinsley is an attorney and Democratic candidate for North Carolina House District 69. She earned a law degree from the University of South Carolina in 2021 and has practiced insurance, real estate and estate law. She lives in Stallings. She has not held elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed on Ballotpedia as receiving recommendations from two Sway voting groups: Fair Map Fight Club and Unburdening The Ballot: Voting Made Easy.

cands.gaps: We could not find where Heidi Sinsley was born or raised, or when she moved to North Carolina. We found no record of any elected office or any bill she sponsored. Her campaign issues page was cut off partway through the Clean Water section, so we did not read what she says on education, veterans, political corruption, justice and law enforcement, worker protections or business. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented public stance from her on data centers or development, and no news coverage of controversies.

qual.background: Attorney since about 2021 who practiced insurance, real estate and estate law, and while in law school worked for the South Carolina House Legislative Oversight Committee, which audits state agencies. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: A lawyer with some legislative-oversight exposure falls in the middle range. She has no prior legislative service, and her law career is short. Her work with the oversight committee came as a law student, and the page does not give her role.
